title: Warehousing
outcomes: Distinguish types of warehouses and licensing rules.
Apply warehousing period and interest provisions.
Apply owner's rights and manufacture in a warehouse.
Apply removal, improper removal and relinquishment rules.

meta.exam_tip: Start every warehousing question by fixing the date of the section 60 order.

concepts.title: Types of warehouses, licensing and bond
body: Warehousing lets importers defer duty by keeping goods in a customs bonded warehouse. Public warehouses (section 57) store anyone's goods; private warehouses (section 58) store only the licensee's goods; special warehouses (section 58A) are under customs lock and hold goods like gold, ship stores and duty-free shop goods.

Licences are not renewed annually, are not transferable, and last until cancellation or surrender. Under section 58B the Commissioner may cancel a licence for contravention after a hearing; goods must then be moved within 7 days of service of the order or as allowed.

Section 59: the importer files an into-bond bill of entry and executes a bond for thrice the assessed duty, undertaking to pay duty, interest and penalties. A consignment-wise or general bond may be executed; the bond continues on transfer, and a transferee executes a fresh bond.
concepts.analogy: Defer duty by keeping goods under bond.
concepts.work: A trader can store imported machines in a public warehouse and pay duty on sale.

concepts.title: Warehousing period and interest
body: Section 61: goods may stay until ex-bonding or consumption (capital goods until ex-bonding) in warehouses with section 65 permission; in other cases, one year from the section 60 order, extendable by the Commissioner by up to one year at a time. Perishable goods may get a shorter period.

Interest at 15% p.a. is charged in other cases on duty deferred beyond 90 days from the section 60 order, till payment. No interest arises in section 65 warehouses. The Board may waive interest or notify goods on which interest runs from day one.
Interest follows duty: if no duty is payable on clearance (e.g. goods re-exported or exempt), no interest is payable (Pratibha Processors).
concepts.analogy: Ninety days free, then fifteen percent a year.
concepts.work: Goods re-exported from a warehouse after six months pay no interest.

concepts.title: Owner's rights and manufacture in a warehouse
body: Section 64 lets the owner inspect, deal with containers to prevent loss or damage, sort, and show the goods for sale.

Section 65 permits manufacturing and other operations in a warehouse with permission. Duty on imported inputs is payable only when resulting goods are cleared for home consumption; no duty on exports. Waste or refuse from operations is either destroyed or charged as if imported in that form; remission is allowed for waste linked to exported products when destroyed.
Since 2016, EOUs, EHTPs and STPs are no longer licensed warehouses and section 65 does not apply to them, though clearances still need approval and duty.
concepts.analogy: Process goods under bond and pay only for domestic clearances.
concepts.work: Imported steel strips turned into knives for export bear no duty.

concepts.title: Removal, improper removal and relinquishment
body: Warehoused goods may be moved to another warehouse (section 67), cleared for home consumption on payment of duty, interest and charges with an ex-bond bill of entry (section 68), or exported without import duty (section 69), e.g. ship stores and duty-free supplies.
Before an order for home clearance, the owner may relinquish title on paying penalties, escaping duty, unless an offence appears to have been committed. Section 71 bars removal except as provided.

Section 72 lets the officer demand full duty, interest and penalties where goods are removed in contravention, not removed after the permitted period, not accounted for, or taken out improperly; the rate is the rate on the date of deemed removal. Section 73 cancels the bond once obligations are met, and section 73A places custody with the warehouse keeper.
concepts.analogy: Three exits: transfer, home clearance or export.
concepts.work: Missing goods found at stock-taking face demand under section 72.

viva.q: What may a warehouse owner do with warehoused goods?
viva.model: Inspect, sort, deal with containers to prevent damage, and show them for sale.

viva.q: When can a licence be cancelled?
viva.model: When the licensee contravenes the Act or licence conditions, after a hearing by the Commissioner.

viva.q: Who has custody of warehoused goods?
What goods typically go to special warehouses?
viva.model: High-value or sensitive goods like gold and duty-free or ship stores, kept under customs lock.

viva.q: Can the owner relinquish warehoused goods?
viva.model: Yes, before the home-clearance order, on paying penalties, unless an offence appears committed.
